697:  * number of elements removed from the stream. The 'approx' option, if non-zero,
698:  * specifies that the trimming must be performed in a approximated way in
699:  * order to maximize performances. This means that the stream may contain
700:  * entries with IDs < 'id' in case of MINID (or more elements than 'maxlen'
701:  * in case of MAXLEN), and elements are only removed if we can remove
702:  * a *whole* node of the radix tree. The elements are removed from the head
703:  * of the stream (older elements).
704:  *
705:  * The function may return zero if:
706:  *
707:  * 1) The minimal entry ID of the stream is already < 'id' (MINID); or
708:  * 2) The stream is already shorter or equal to the specified max length (MAXLEN); or
709:  * 3) The 'approx' option is true and the head node did not have enough elements
710:  *    to be deleted.
711:  *
712:  * args->limit is the maximum number of entries to delete. The purpose is to
713:  * prevent this function from taking to long.
714:  * If 'limit' is 0 then we do not limit the number of deleted entries.
715:  * Much like the 'approx', if 'limit' is smaller than the number of entries
716:  * that should be trimmed, there is a chance we will still have entries with
717:  * IDs < 'id' (or number of elements >= maxlen in case of MAXLEN).
718:  */
719: int64_t streamTrim(stream *s, streamAddTrimArgs *args) {
720:     size_t maxlen = args->maxlen;
721:     streamID *id = &args->minid;
722:     int approx = args->approx_trim;
723:     int64_t limit = args->limit;
724:     int trim_strategy = args->trim_strategy;
725: 
726:     if (trim_strategy == TRIM_STRATEGY_NONE)
727:         return 0;
728: 
729:     raxIterator ri;
730:     raxStart(&ri,s->rax);
731:     raxSeek(&ri,"^",NULL,0);
732: 
733:     int64_t deleted = 0;
734:     while (raxNext(&ri)) {
735:         if (trim_strategy == TRIM_STRATEGY_MAXLEN && s->length <= maxlen)
736:             break;
737: 
738:         unsigned char *lp = ri.data, *p = lpFirst(lp);
739:         int64_t entries = lpGetInteger(p);
740: 
741:         /* Check if we exceeded the amount of work we could do */
742:         if (limit && (deleted + entries) > limit)
743:             break;
744: 
745:         /* Check if we can remove the whole node. */
746:         int remove_node;
747:         streamID master_id = {0}; /* For MINID */
748:         if (trim_strategy == TRIM_STRATEGY_MAXLEN) {
749:             remove_node = s->length - entries >= maxlen;
750:         } else {
751:             /* Read the master ID from the radix tree key. */
752:             streamDecodeID(ri.key, &master_id);
753: 
754:             /* Read last ID. */
755:             streamID last_id;
756:             lpGetEdgeStreamID(lp, 0, &master_id, &last_id);
757: 
758:             /* We can remove the entire node id its last ID < 'id' */
759:             remove_node = streamCompareID(&last_id, id) < 0;
760:         }
761: 
762:         if (remove_node) {
763:             lpFree(lp);
764:             raxRemove(s->rax,ri.key,ri.key_len,NULL);
765:             raxSeek(&ri,">=",ri.key,ri.key_len);
766:             s->length -= entries;
767:             deleted += entries;
768:             continue;
769:         }
770: 
771:         /* If we cannot remove a whole element, and approx is true,
772:          * stop here. */
773:         if (approx) break;
774: 
775:         /* Now we have to trim entries from within 'lp' */
776:         int64_t deleted_from_lp = 0;
777: 
778:         p = lpNext(lp, p); /* Skip deleted field. */
779:         p = lpNext(lp, p); /* Skip num-of-fields in the master entry. */
780: 
781:         /* Skip all the master fields. */
782:         int64_t master_fields_count = lpGetInteger(p);
783:         p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip the first field. */
784:         for (int64_t j = 0; j < master_fields_count; j++)
785:             p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip all master fields. */
786:         p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip the zero master entry terminator. */
787: 
788:         /* 'p' is now pointing to the first entry inside the listpack.
789:          * We have to run entry after entry, marking entries as deleted
790:          * if they are already not deleted. */
791:         while (p) {
792:             /* We keep a copy of p (which point to flags part) in order to
793:              * update it after (and if) we actually remove the entry */
794:             unsigned char *pcopy = p;
795: 
796:             int flags = lpGetInteger(p);
797:             p = lpNext(lp, p); /* Skip flags. */
798:             int to_skip;
799: 
800:             int ms_delta = lpGetInteger(p);
801:             p = lpNext(lp, p); /* Skip ID ms delta */
802:             int seq_delta = lpGetInteger(p);
803:             p = lpNext(lp, p); /* Skip ID seq delta */
804: 
805:             streamID currid = {0}; /* For MINID */
806:             if (trim_strategy == TRIM_STRATEGY_MINID) {
807:                 currid.ms = master_id.ms + ms_delta;
808:                 currid.seq = master_id.seq + seq_delta;
809:             }
810: 
811:             int stop;
812:             if (trim_strategy == TRIM_STRATEGY_MAXLEN) {
813:                 stop = s->length <= maxlen;
814:             } else {
815:                 /* Following IDs will definitely be greater because the rax
816:                  * tree is sorted, no point of continuing. */
817:                 stop = streamCompareID(&currid, id) >= 0;
818:             }
819:             if (stop)
820:                 break;
821: 
822:             if (flags & STREAM_ITEM_FLAG_SAMEFIELDS) {
823:                 to_skip = master_fields_count;
824:             } else {
825:                 to_skip = lpGetInteger(p); /* Get num-fields. */
826:                 p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip num-fields. */
827:                 to_skip *= 2; /* Fields and values. */
828:             }
829: 
830:             while(to_skip--) p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip the whole entry. */
831:             p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip the final lp-count field. */
832: 
833:             /* Mark the entry as deleted. */
834:             if (!(flags & STREAM_ITEM_FLAG_DELETED)) {
835:                 intptr_t delta = p - lp;
836:                 flags |= STREAM_ITEM_FLAG_DELETED;
837:                 lp = lpReplaceInteger(lp, &pcopy, flags);
838:                 deleted_from_lp++;
839:                 s->length--;
840:                 p = lp + delta;
841:             }
842:         }
843:         deleted += deleted_from_lp;
844: 
845:         /* Now we the entries/deleted counters. */
846:         p = lpFirst(lp);
847:         lp = lpReplaceInteger(lp,&p,entries-deleted_from_lp);
848:         p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip deleted field. */
849:         int64_t marked_deleted = lpGetInteger(p);
850:         lp = lpReplaceInteger(lp,&p,marked_deleted+deleted_from_lp);
851:         p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip num-of-fields in the master entry. */
852: 
853:         /* Here we should perform garbage collection in case at this point
854:          * there are too many entries deleted inside the listpack. */
855:         entries -= deleted_from_lp;
856:         marked_deleted += deleted_from_lp;
857:         if (entries + marked_deleted > 10 && marked_deleted > entries/2) {
858:             /* TODO: perform a garbage collection. */
859:         }
860: 
861:         /* Update the listpack with the new pointer. */
862:         raxInsert(s->rax,ri.key,ri.key_len,lp,NULL);
863: 
864:         break; /* If we are here, there was enough to delete in the current
865:                   node, so no need to go to the next node. */
866:     }
867: 
868:     raxStop(&ri);
869:     return deleted;
870: }

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `streamTrim` (src/t_stream.c:800-802): the ID deltas stored in the listpack are 64-bit values, but they were read into `int` (32-bit) variables. When an entry's timestamp far exceeds the node's master ID (e.g. `10-1` followed by auto-generated IDs), the delta overflows and wraps negative, so `currid` was computed as lower than the MINID threshold and every entry got marked deleted.

The fix changes `ms_delta`/`seq_delta` to `int64_t`. Verified with the issue's exact repro (XTRIM now deletes only the entries below the threshold) and all `unit/type/stream` and `unit/type/stream-cgroups` tests pass.
